references.text: Moses reminds the people that God humbled them, let them hunger, and then gave them manna to eat, teaching them that man does not live by bread alone. This expands on the purpose of manna as a test.
Manna is described as food unknown to their fathers, given to humble and test the people. This confirms the testing aspect from Exodus 16:4.
Nehemiah refers to God giving bread from heaven when the people were hungry, a direct reference to the miracle of manna.
The psalm tells how God rained down manna upon the people and gave them grain from heaven—the bread of angels. A poetic retelling of the manna miracle.
The psalm mentions that God satisfied the people with bread from heaven, a praise of the manna miracle.
Jesus quotes that their fathers ate manna in the wilderness and explains that it was not Moses, but the Father who gives the true bread from heaven.
Jesus contrasts the manna their fathers ate with Himself as the living bread from heaven that gives eternal life.
Paul mentions that all their fathers ate the same spiritual food, a reference to the manna in the wilderness.
The promise of hidden manna to the one who overcomes connects to the manna from heaven as a symbol of spiritual nourishment.
A direct narrative continuation explaining the purpose of preserving manna as a testimony to God's provision.
A thematic parallel contrasting humanity's test of obedience with God's test of faith in His almighty power.
A deep thematic connection through the concept of 'test' (nasah), showing God's intent to test the people toward obedience and reverence for Him.
